text: The owner-ordered re-order (fallback1 = minimax-m3.1-flash-free, fallback2 = mimo-v2.6-flash) is executable on the live canonical Hermes config with a reversible, digest-guarded apply that touches only the fallback_providers block.
Both new arms can actually serve through the transport the Hermes fallback path will use for them.

Re-ordering the live chain requires no change to the HGK control-plane declaration surfaces, because the registry records the live config as NON_AUTHORITATIVE and binds no pointer to its fallback_providers.
The owner order, read literally, also re-binds the HGK registry's declared PLAN lane chain, because that chain names the same two models as the live chain's first two entries.
After the re-order, the first SERVABLE fallback arm is mimo-v2.6-flash (not minimax-m3.1-flash-free) because the runtime skips a chain entry that resolves to the backend that just failed.
The two new ids are routable but absent from the curated static provider catalog, which is a material regression for the chain.
